Looking to the short controversy involved in the matter at this stage and the order that this Court proposes to pass, notices to respondents are being dispensed with and if the respondents are aggrieved by the order, they would be at liberty to file review of this order.
These appeals are by land losers and involve similar short question, therefore, they are being decided by this common order.
For the sake of convenience, facts are taken from AA No.15 of 2026.

2. Initially, the Divisional Commissioner, Jabalpur being Arbitrator had passed an award under National Highways Act 1956, which was challenged before the District Court under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and vide order dated 22.07.2022, the District Court had arrived at a conclusion

that the quantum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:11062 AA No.15/2026, 16/2026, 17/2026 & 14/2026 compensation has not been arrived at an appropriate rate by the Land Acquisition Officer and also found that the award of the Arbitrator is contrary to the basic notions of law and justice and, therefore, set aside the award but looking to the position that in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NHAI v. M. Hakeem, reported in (2021) 9 SCC 1, the award cannot be modified but can only be set aside, therefore, the award was set aside by the District Court and was remanded back to the Arbitrator.

sentences.text: 3. Upon remand, the matter was heard by the Collector because in the intervening period, the jurisdiction to act as Arbitrator in matters containing land acquisitions under National Highways Act, had been conferred upon the Collector of the District and the Collector then passed the fresh award dated 16.05.2024 and the Collector upheld the earlier award holding that the earlier assessment of compensation was proper.

4. The said fresh award was challenged before the District Court again by filing application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 and this time, the District Court has passed the order dated 11.10.2025,
holding that once the District Court has already remanded the matter back to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:11062 AA No.15/2026, 16/2026, 17/2026 & 14/2026 Arbitrator,
therefore, against the fresh award passed after remand, the Court does not have any jurisdiction to entertain application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996.

sentences.text: The aforesaid order deserves to be set aside because there is no bar in the Act of 1996 that once having set aside the award and the Arbitrator having passed a fresh award, then the said award would be immune from challenge under Section 34 of the Act of 1996.

The order passed by the District Court dated 11.10.2025 holding that once the District Court remands the matter to the Arbitrator, then the fresh award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be challenged under Section 34 of the Act of 1996, is not backed by any provision of the Act of 1996.
The legal remedy available to a party cannot be scuttled unless the remedy is barred in the Act.
The Act is silent on the aspect but it grants a remedy to challenge the award under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 on the limited grounds as available under the said provision.

The District Court, therefore, was having jurisdiction to entertain challenge to the fresh award as per the limited grounds available under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 and it could not be said that the District Court would apply mind only once in the matter and once it has set aside the award and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:11062 AA No.15/2026, 16/2026, 17/2026 & 14/2026 remanded back the matter to the Arbitrator
, then the fresh award passed after remand would be immune from challenge.

6. Recently, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gayatri Balasamy v.
ISG Novasoft Technologies Ltd., reported in (2025) 7 SCC 1, as contained in the majority opinion in para 87, has held that when the award is severable, the invalid portion can be severed from the valid portion of the award and limited powers may be exercised even to modify the award by the Court under Sections 34 and 37 of the Act of 1996.

8. Appeals are accordingly disposed of.
